title: Southern Yan
capsule: Southern Yan was a Xianbei-ruled dynastic state of the Sixteen Kingdoms era, established in 398 by Murong De after his branch of the Murong clan was expelled from the north by Later Yan's collapse under Northern Wei pressure. Murong De declared himself emperor at Huatai before relocating the capital to Guanggu (modern Qingzhou, Shandong), where the kingdom controlled much of the Shandong peninsula. His nephew and successor Murong Chao (r. 405–410) proved a less capable ruler; Jin general Liu Yu besieged Guanggu in 409 and in 410 captured and executed Murong Chao, extinguishing the state.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Southern Yan's core territory in Shandong is attested in Chinese annals, but precise boundary data for the short-lived kingdom is limited to textual sources and approximate on any map.
